This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst. Cleanups underway after Hurricane Isaias, now a post-tropical storm, left at least four people dead and hundreds of thousands of customers without electricity.
NPR's Debbie Elliott reports the storm made landfall last night near Destin, Florida as a Category 2 hurricane.
Hurricane Isaias came ashore with 105-mile-an-hour winds, a five-foot storm surge and heavy rainfall, causing damage from the Alabama Gulf Coast into the Florida Panhandle.
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis says emergency crews are working now to clear down trees and power lines and repair damaged water systems.
It's still a very hazardous situation. All the assets are there to get the power back on, make sure all the roads are clean and safe, and that's being done.
But just please continue to exercise caution in the next couple of days.
The remnants of Isaias are moving across the southeast with a risk of flash flooding. Debbie Elliott, NPR News, Crestview, Florida.
Anthropic is reporting fresh incidents of A.I. bots doing things they weren't supposed to do, including sending the Philadelphia Police a false tip about an unsolved homicide.
And here's John Ruich reports.
Anthropic listed four new cases where artificial intelligence agents went off script, and the Philadelphia Police Department confirms that it was involved in one of them.
It says Anthropic recently told the department that a bot undergoing testing had submitted a false homicide tip back in July through a public tip form online.
The submission was flagged as spam and never forwarded for investigation.
Anthropic says an agent also broke into a server at a university that it wasn't supposed to. Another got around paywalls to access data.
The company says it also found agents using URL shortening tools online to get around blocks.
The cases are the latest in a growing list of examples of A.I. agents from a range of companies taking actions that have raised concern about loss of control.
John Ruich, NPR News.
Consumer spending kept rising in September, according to the Bank of America Institute and based on consumer spending data.
And here's Stephen Bassaha reports lower income households saw some of the fastest spending growth.
Overall, spending grew 6.2 percent compared with last September.
The Bank of America Institute's David Tinsley said bad vibes about the economy have not stopped shoppers.
Spending is remarkably resilient for consumers.
Spending growth by lower income households has outpaced all but the highest earners.
That's a change from how much they lagged other groups earlier this year and last.
That is probably the single biggest change we've seen in our data, say over the last three or four months.
Spending growth is outpacing inflation and growing faster than it was at this time last year, both for essential and discretionary items.
Stephen Bassaha, NPR News, Birmingham, Alabama.
You're listening to NPR News.
Police in Erie, Pennsylvania, say nine people are dead after a shooting in the city last night.
And here's Shonda Lee Stuster has more.
The shooting took place near Perry and Seventh Streets, according to police.
They have shared little details about what happened, but say investigators believe the deaths occurred before law enforcement arrived.
Police say they are gathering more information and seeking a search warrant.
Erie Mayor Daria Devlin said in a statement Friday her heart is heavy and her thoughts are with the families and others involved.
Shonda Lee Stuster, NPR News.
A federal proposal to gut the standards for the country's largest early education program closed to public comment this week.
Tens of thousands of people posted their concerns as NPR's Sequoia Carilla reports.
The Trump administration's proposed changes to the Head Start program garnered more than 40,000 comments over the last two months.
The administration says the move to take 133 pages of guidelines and reduce it to only a handful is meant to reduce administrative burden on Head Start centers.
But advocates say the move will undermine the program's standard of care.
The six-year-old anti-poverty program provides preschool and childcare along with meals and support services for qualifying families.
The program serves more than 700,000 kids each year from birth to age five.
The proposal now goes back to the Trump administration to reply to public comment.
Sequoia Carillo, NPR News.
And I'm Janine Hurst, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
